jobs.title: GTM Data Analyst
jobs.description_text: Netic is the AI revenue engine for essential services who are the backbone of the American economy. With $43M in funding from Founders Fund, Greylock, Hanabi, and Dylan Field who led our Series B, we helped our customers book hundreds of thousands of jobs across services industries in North America. There are now companies operating entirely AI-first on Netic. You’ll join our team with relentless builders from Scale, Databricks, HRT, Meta, MIT, Stanford, and Harvard in bringing frontier AI to the physical economy, where the problems are hard, the data is complex, and the impact is immediate and tangible. THE ROLE You'll be Netic's first dedicated go-to-market data hire. Nobody owns our account and contact data end to end yet: you will. You'll define the data standards, build the models and checks that keep them accurate, and give the team a foundation for territories, routing, forecasting and commissions. This is an analyst role with operational ownership. You'll spend as much time writing SQL and building models as you do fixing the processes that create bad data in the first place. jobs.title: 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist
jobs.description_text: ABOUT NIANTIC SPATIAL We are building for the >80% of economic activity that happens beyond the reach of screens. AI has learned from the text, images and video online, but it still lacks an accurate understanding of physical space. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist to join our Research Team in London. Our team researches and builds the 3D reconstruction technology behind Niantic Spatial's platform. jobs.description_text: ABOUT ODYS At Odys, we’re mobilizing power, with Hybrid Power Systems developed for aerospace and in-demand everywhere. It’s the kind of mission diversity that demands a fresh way of thinking. We began with an early bet on hybrid, when the mobility industry was focused on batteries. jobs.description_text: HEAD OF PRODUCT MARKETING Outmarket AI · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to the SVP of Marketing ABOUT OUTMARKET Insurance still runs on manual work. Most policies are sold through agents and brokers, and the people who know the work best are buried in the documents: checking policies line by line, comparing quotes, building proposals, on nights and weekends. We think that's backwards. The best people in insurance should spend their time advising clients. Outmarket, the AI platform built for insurance, makes that possible. Account teams drop in their documents and get back finished work to review, with every finding linked to the page it came from. Outmarket connects to the systems they already use. jobs.description_text: The Role We’re hiring a Product Manager to own how customers write, test, and ship the control programs that run their hardware. Those programs are written in RevelCode, our domain-specific language for hardware control, and you’ll own both the language experience and the IDE we’re building for it. The people writing RevelCode are test and controls engineers, and what they write executes against physical systems. A confusing compiler error or a slow test loop costs more than time here. It raises the chance a mistake reaches hardware. What You’ll Do - Own the full workflow for writing, testing, deploying, and monitoring RevelCode: editing and deploying configurations to the runtime, unit testing control logic before it ships, version control, and dashboard generation - Own RevelCode usability end to end: syntax, snippets, completion, diagnostics, and the compiler errors customers report as the most confusing - Run discovery with customers and operators, including at air-gapped sites, to learn which editor features they actually depend on rather than which ones they’d claim to miss - Develop an IDE strategy that engineering agrees with. It should say what our IDE does better than a general-purpose editor for control programs, and what customers give up for anything we don’t rebuild Who You Are - You’ve built developer tools and you use them critically. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market. THE TEAM AND ROLE SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves. We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H. This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code.
